problemsHighlight: We make sure the firmware does your hardware justice.

hardware.title: PCB Design & Board Bring-up
hardware.description: From schematic to a board that boots, with hardware and firmware under one roof.
hardware.longDescription: We design boards in KiCad (power paths, battery charging, USB-C, ESP32 and RP2040) and bring them up: first power-on, clocks, peripherals and drivers. Because the same team does the hardware and the firmware, nobody has to guess which side a bug is on.
points: KiCad schematic and layout, 2 and 4 layers
Production files for JLCPCB: Gerbers, BOM and pick-and-place
Bring-up, first drivers and a written bring-up report

firmware.title: RTOS & Embedded Linux Firmware
firmware.description: Firmware and connectivity that stay up in the field.
firmware.longDescription: FreeRTOS on Cortex-M and ESP32, embedded Linux on Raspberry Pi and custom hardware, and the connectivity in between: Ethernet, Wi-Fi and MQTT. We write the drivers, chase down the hard bugs (memory, timing, networking) and leave you with code your team can maintain.
points: Drivers, RTOS tasks and protocol stacks
Ethernet, Wi-Fi and MQTT device-to-cloud links
Debugging crashes, memory leaks and timing issues
firmware.proof: Core developers of a production i.MX RT IoT gateway, with 199 releases shipped since 2025.

updates.title: Secure Updates & CRA Readiness
updates.description: Field updates that can’t brick a device, ready for the Cyber Resilience Act.
updates.longDescription: Since September 2026 the EU Cyber Resilience Act requires manufacturers to report actively exploited vulnerabilities, and from December 2027 connected products must ship with secure updates, an SBOM and a defined support period. We build the update path (signed images, A/B slots, automatic rollback) and set up the SBOM and vulnerability-handling process around it.
points: CRA gap assessment with a prioritized roadmap
Signed A/B updates with automatic rollback
SBOM generated in CI and a vulnerability-handling runbook
updates.proof: Built over-the-air bootloader and firmware updates for a production IoT gateway, and an A/B loader with automatic rollback for a Raspberry Pi kiosk fleet.

modernization.title: Firmware Modernization
modernization.description: Make legacy firmware testable, maintainable and safe to change.
modernization.longDescription: Old toolchains, no tests, and one person who understands the code. We audit legacy firmware, move it step by step to modern C++ (or Rust where it fits), and add tests that run on a PC and on real hardware in CI, so changes stop being scary.
points: Code audit with a prioritized report
Host-side unit tests and hardware-in-the-loop tests in CI
Incremental rewrites to modern C++ or Rust
modernization.proof: Built hardware-in-the-loop update tests that run in Jenkins on every change to a production IoT gateway.

ai.title: AI for Engineering Teams
ai.description: Get your firmware team productive with AI coding tools, with every change still verified on real hardware.
ai.longDescription: Hands-on workshops and repository setup for embedded teams adopting tools like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot: project knowledge files, review guardrails, and workflows where every AI-made change is verified on real hardware. Also available: Software Engineering in Practice, a three-part training on foundations, resilience and production.
points: Repository setup: agent instructions, knowledge bases and guardrails
Software Engineering in Practice training with certificates
ai.proof: Set up the agent instructions and knowledge base for a production firmware project, now used day to day by its developers.

fintech.title: FinTech & Payment Systems
fintech.description: Payment terminals, vending machines and kiosks that handle money reliably.
fintech.longDescription: Payment and vending devices have to work every time: a failed transaction costs money and trust. We build firmware for payment terminals, vending machines and self-service kiosks, covering payment flows, stock tracking, secure communication and field updates that don’t take a machine offline.

manufacturing.title: Industrial & Manufacturing
manufacturing.description: Connected machines that report what they’re doing and keep running.
manufacturing.longDescription: Factory equipment runs for years and can’t stop for a firmware bug. We build controllers and gateways that collect machine data, send it over Ethernet or MQTT, and keep running through power cuts, network drops and updates.

defense.title: Defense & Aerospace
defense.description: Predictable, verifiable software for high-stakes programs.
defense.longDescription: In defense and aerospace, software has to be predictable, tested and documented. We bring experience from avionics programs (deterministic real-time behaviour, rigorous testing and traceable documentation) to every project.

automotive.title: Automotive & Mobility
automotive.description: Firmware and lab tooling for vehicle development.
automotive.longDescription: Vehicle development runs on tooling that has to work every time: flashing, netbooting and test benches. Our open-source TFTP server and client are used by automotive engineers, and we build firmware and lab tooling with real-time and reliability requirements in mind.

contact.mailNote: Submitting opens your email app with your message filled in. We reply within one business day.

industries.title: Embedded Software Expertise Across Industries
industries.description: Firmware for payment and vending devices, industrial machines, defense and aerospace systems, and automotive development tooling.

blog.title: Insights on Embedded Software Engineering
blog.description: Articles and tutorials covering embedded systems, RTOS, Linux, IoT, and firmware development best practices, with practical insights from real-world projects.

tools.title: Embedded Software Tools for Firmware Engineers
tools.description: A collection of web-based tools for embedded and firmware development, including CRC calculators, protocol utilities, and debugging helpers.

kiosk.title: Field updates that can’t brick a device
kiosk.challenge: A fleet of Raspberry Pi kiosks needed remote updates and provisioning, with nobody on site to recover a device when an update goes wrong.
kiosk.work: Built the loader that supervises the kiosk software: A/B app slots with automatic rollback after repeated failures, a 21-step provisioning script that is safe to re-run, a systemd watchdog, and a Jenkins + Docker pipeline that checks every release before it ships.
kiosk.result: 18 releases over 18 months, each rolled out remotely and rolled back automatically if it fails.

tftpd.title: A TFTP server automotive engineers build on
tftpd.challenge: U-Boot netbooting and board flashing need a small, dependable TFTP server and client that runs on any machine in the lab.
tftpd.work: Wrote rs-tftpd from scratch in pure Rust, with RFC 2347–2349 and 7440 option support and a matching client, and maintain it as an open-source project.
tftpd.result: Packaged for NixOS and openSUSE, with contributions from engineers at Renault Software Labs, Ampere and Nokia. Renault uses the client as a library, and its duplicate-packets option cut an Apache NuttX network boot from 4 minutes to 20 seconds.

notSure.title: Not sure which fits?
notSure.description: Tell us about your device and we’ll suggest where to start.

cra.title: Cyber Resilience Act Self-Check for Firmware
cra.description: A free 15-question check of how ready your connected product’s firmware is for the EU Cyber Resilience Act: updates, SBOM, vulnerability reporting and secure defaults.
cra.intro: Fifteen questions about one product. Answers stay in your browser, nothing is sent anywhere.
cra.resultIncomplete: Answer all questions to see your full result.
cra.noGaps: No gaps found. Keep the SBOM, reporting process and support period up to date with every release.
cra.ctaText: Want help closing these gaps? We build secure update paths, SBOM pipelines and vulnerability-handling processes for embedded products.
cra.readMore: Read: what the CRA means for your firmware
cra.disclaimer: This check is a starting point, not legal advice. The CRA has more requirements than these questions cover.

sbom.title: Online SBOM Viewer for CycloneDX and SPDX
sbom.description: Open a CycloneDX or SPDX JSON SBOM in your browser: list components and licenses, and spot entries missing a version, license, supplier or package URL.
sbom.intro: Drop a CycloneDX or SPDX JSON file, or paste it below. The file is read in your browser and never uploaded.
sbom.drop: Drop an SBOM file here or click to choose one
sbom.errorFormat: This doesn’t look like a CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM.
sbom.name: Name
sbom.hint: Package URLs (purl) and versions are what vulnerability scanners match against. Entries without them are invisible to CVE monitoring.
